t: Tankers hit by mines in Hormuz as Iran sets seven conditions for Washington
x: Tehran says at least five tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, as the Pentagon stands ready for a resumption of fighting. Through Qatar, Iran has passed a proposal on its nuclear programme to the United States.

t: Paraguay's president, Santiago Peña, resigns and is impeached within minutes
x: Brought down by the collapse of Ueno, a digital bank that claimed more than 60% of the country's adults as customers, the head of state announced his departure on Thursday. Deputies voted to impeach him straight afterwards.

t: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks, Russian and Ukrainian envoys meet at the White House
x: Melania Trump brought together envoys from both countries in Washington on Thursday, with no progress announced. On the ground, Moscow is targeting Ukraine's energy and logistics networks while Kyiv steps up drone attacks on Russian refineries.

t: Herzog to name Israel's next prime minister on Sunday, with Gadi Eisenkot in pole position
x: With 67 of the 120 members of the Knesset behind him, the former army chief awaits the mandate the president is due to hand out on 8 November. In Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, down to 46 backers, some cry "stolen" election.

t: Somalia's Supreme Court rules the extension of the president's term unlawful
x: The country's highest court on Thursday gave the parties thirty days to reach agreement and ninety days to hold elections. The day before, the head of state, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, had sacked the chief justice.

t: Midterms: Democrats retake Congress as Trump pays the price for the Iran war
x: After a historic election night, the opposition has seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The president admits that the conflict with Tehran weighed heavily on the vote.

t: Washington and Tehran: fears of a return to war after the US vote
x: Qatar is trying to secure an interim deal before the United States resumes its strikes. Eight months into the conflict, the Strait of Hormuz remains almost closed and oil is above $100 a barrel.

t: Russia strikes civilians and the power grid in Ukraine ahead of new talks
x: A Russian strike on a school where humanitarian aid was being handed out has killed at least 43 people in the Zaporizhzhia region, as Moscow keeps pounding the power grid. Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

t: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot wins the backing of most MPs against Benjamin Netanyahu
x: Abandoned by the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party, Benjamin Netanyahu gathers only 46 recommendations, against 67 for his rival, who is backed by the Arab parties. In Gaza, a year after the ceasefire, Israeli strikes still claim lives almost every day.

t: In Sudan, a drone war is strangling civilians
x: More than three years into the conflict, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces are stepping up strikes on infrastructure. The crisis is now spilling over into neighbouring Ethiopia.
